sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F1][F8][F145].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 2.9% in FY2020 and 5.2% in FY2024, then rebounded 9.8% in FY2025 [D61][D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline came from lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [P35].
Operating margin swung from 15.5% in FY2021 to 41.3% in FY2023, then settled at 32.1% in FY2025 [F20][F22][F24].
The FY2021 trough reflected a $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity [P63][P68].
FPL supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue rose on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel recovery [P21].
NEER's results increased on higher earnings from new investments, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against 7.7% for revenue, but net income compounded at only 0.4% [F146][F145][F147].
Diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year as the share count rose 0.6% in FY2025 [F149][D251].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits 1.8pp above the window median of 30.3% and well above the 15.5% low [F24][D300][D298].
Operating expenses grew 10.0% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025, so incremental operating margin was 34.8% [D249][D236][D256].
Depreciation and amortization rose $951 million, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [P16].
Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% even as operating margin edged up 0.3pp [D248][F40][D247].
Corporate and Other results fell $1,256 million on unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025, below the 2.16x of FY2019 [F64][F32][D227][D17].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025 while net income fell 1.6% [D241][D238].
The shift from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Investing outflow of $23.9 billion dwarfed operating cash flow, funded largely by $23.4 billion of debt issued [F72][F64][X90].
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025, down from net cash of -$34.3 billion in FY2018, a seventh straight year of deterioration [D231][D9][R2].
Net cash was -357.4% of revenue, worse than the utilities peer median of -228.4% and the 0th percentile of four peers [D232][D315][D314].
Long-term debt grew 18.8% a year against 6.9% for equity, and the current ratio of 0.60x is still below 1.0x [F156][F157][F128].
Dividends of $4.68 billion were the only capital return, with no buybacks, while the diluted share count rose 0.6% [X82][D233][D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025, though that is the window high [F128][D305][R1].
Net cash has fallen for seven consecutive years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025, as capex outran cash flow [D9][D231][R2].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of -17.7% reflects clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million at NEER [D226][P11][R4].
FY2019 operating expenses were later restated to $14.3 billion from $13.9 billion, a data-quality caveat on that year's margin [X18][R5].
If operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median in the FY2026 10-K, the FY2023 spike looks structural rather than cyclical [D300].
Net cash falling further below the FY2025 level of -$92.2 billion would extend the seven-year trend and pressure the 0th-percentile peer rank [D231][D314].
Operating cash flow below the FY2025 level of $12.5 billion would confirm the conversion decline from 2.16x in FY2019 [F64][D17].
